extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark comprising 20,000 conflicts evenly distributed between language-language and vision-language paradigms to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in recognizing conflicting commands. The benchmark includes 8 tasks: RuleConflict, AttributeConflict, ExclusionConflict, ForbiddenConflict (language-language), and OCRConflict, FigureConflict, GeometricConflict, SemanticConflict (vision-language).
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang
extraction.publisher: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Fudan University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is constructed using a novel automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate, which leverages programs and large language models. AutoCreate starts from several task-relevant seeds and maintains a seed pool. During each cycle, AutoCreate includes two branches: the language branch and the vision branch. Each branch consists of a generator and a decorator. The cleaner excludes data that does not meet the standards. The data is fed into the seed pool for the next round after a quality check by human experts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: For language-language conflicts, the raw data is generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) based on manually input seeds. For vision-language conflicts, SemanticConflict uses the ImageNet dataset as the source, while other tasks generate synthetic images based on LLM-generated content.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For FigureConflict, numerical data is manipulated by changing the maximum value to the minimum value. For GeometricConflict, attribute descriptions are exchanged to introduce confusion. For SemanticConflict, correct labels in questions are substituted with similar but different objects.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The generation process comprises two loops: the Language Loop and the Visual Loop. Each loop originates from the Seed Pool and is sequentially processed by a fully automated Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner. The Generator creates initial language/vision data, the Decorator creates self-contradictions in the generated data, and the Cleaner removes data that does not meet quality standards. Both human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset. The resulting high-quality dataset is then refined to extract new seeds for re-entry into the seed pool.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts rigorously checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset. Three levels of splits were manually provided according to the occurring frequency of conflict types: SCI-Core (1%), SCI-Base (10%), and SCI-All (100%).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Evaluation is first conducted by human experts. LLMs (specifically GPT-4) are employed as evaluation agents for efficiency. An experiment demonstrates that LLMs as evaluation agents align with human experts, with Spearman correlation coefficient of 0.881 for GPT-4V, 0.999 for LLaVA-1.5, and 0.854 for Gemini, with concordance rates of 94%, 99%, and 97% respectively.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large Language Models (LLMs) including ChatGLM, ChatGPT, GPT-4, Llama 2, and GLM-4 were used for automatic dataset generation. GPT-4 was used as an evaluation agent.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work has significant social implications. It provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies. The AutoCreate framework facilitates the creation of diverse instruction datasets, promoting inclusivity in AI research. By improving dissonance detection, the approach boosts LMM performance and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems, essential for societal integration.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms. More modalities will be included in future work. No fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree. The study does not provide a detailed analysis of the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to detect conflicting commands. It can be used for testing and benchmarking LMMs' self-awareness and ability to recognize instruction dissonance. The benchmark facilitates qualitative evaluation through three difficulty levels (SCI-Core, SCI-Base, SCI-All).
